title: Choose the blog’s reading structure
question: Which page structure best helps visitors discover Sayed’s automotive work and interests in content creation? All three keep the current site identity and calm, readable article text.

options.label: Field Notes
options.lineage: An inspector’s notebook, adapted as a personal editorial journal
options.thesis: One featured dispatch leads into a clear stream of notes on cars, quality, and making content.
options.viewport: A strong masthead and featured essay lead the reading column; a slim side index points to automotive, quality, and creator topics.
options.risk: The notebook language could become too technical if annotations crowd the articles.

options.label: Open Garage Index
options.lineage: An independent motoring journal with a browsable editorial archive
options.thesis: A personal introduction sits beside one lead story, with a tidy archive grouped by subject below.
options.viewport: The reader meets Sayed and the lead article first, then sees distinct article rows for cars, quality, and content creation.
options.risk: A conventional magazine grid could make the personal voice feel secondary.

options.label: Two Lenses Journal
options.lineage: A field guide that connects a subject’s craft with the stories made about it
options.thesis: Two clear reading paths connect automotive quality and content creation without blending their topics.
options.viewport: A personal opening branches into two labeled article tracks, then rejoins in a short profile and chronological archive.
options.risk: Separate tracks may fragment the page if shared context and chronology are hard to find.
